title: Clinical Guide: Anophthalmia, Microphthalmia & Socket Disorders
summary: An exhaustive clinical overview covering the developmental failure of the globe, indications for surgical eye removal, and the comprehensive management of the anophthalmic socket and its associated complications.

branches: Anophthalmia: Absence of an eye within the orbit
1° Anophthalmia: Complete failure of any ocular tissue to develop
2° Anophthalmia: Partial development which then halts, leaving a very small microphthalmic eye
Degenerative Anophthalmia: Partially developed eye regresses

sections.title: Developmental Treatment Strategy
content: Early treatment: Use of conformers and orbit expanders (Normal development of orbit and lids depends on globe presence)
Age < 2 years: Hydrophilic orbital expanders (must be replaced every few weeks)
Subsequent Phase: Replace with painted prostheses
Long-term: Continue treatment until the face has fully developed

sections.title: Specialized Management Needs
content: Special conformers: Available for microphthalmic eyes where limited vision is preserved; improves cosmesis without obstructing vision
Surgery: Used to reduce orbital asymmetry
Multidisciplinary Team: Paediatric ophthalmologist, orbital surgeon, and orbital prosthesist (among others)

sections.title: Surgical Classifications
content: Enucleation: Eye removal, leaving extraocular muscles (eOMs) intact
Evisceration: Eye content removal, leaving sclera and eOMs
Exenteration: Removal of eye and parts of the orbit (lids, orbital tissue, bone)

sections.title: Orbital Implant Principles
sections.content: Placement of an orbital implant (acrylic or hydroxyapatite) is almost always performed in conjunction with enucleation/evisceration. The principal of implant placement is to choose the largest possible for that patient’s socket.

branches: Definition: Features resulting from deficient, shrunken volume of orbital tissues surrounding a socket
Superior sulcus deformity (hollowing above the upper eyelid)

sections.title: PESS Treatment: Inadequate Volume
content: Prosthetist to modify or replace existing prosthesis
Exchange orbital implant for one of a larger volume
Subperiosteal orbital floor implant
Orbital injection of filler material (i.e. hyaluronic acid-based)
Dermis fat graft: Autogenous dermis and subdermal fat (e.g. from abdomen, left inguinal region, or buttocks)

sections.title: PESS Treatment: Abnormal Lid Position
content: Lateral or medial tarsal strip
Levator resection

sections.title: The Discharging Socket
content: Small amount of discharge is common and needs differentiation from socket infection or Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis (GPC)
Causes: Socket dryness, presence of prosthesis, resulting abrasion of socket conjunctiva
Infection Hallmark: Recurrent discharge resistant to multiple drops
Infection Hallmark: Implant discomfort (to touch)
Infection Hallmark: Recurrent pyogenic granuloma

sections.title: Management of Infection and Discharge
content: Ensure regular cleaning and polishing of prosthesis (e.g. annual)
Advise patient not to remove prosthesis too frequently
Ensure no exposed sutures or implant exposure
Short course of topical lubricants, antibiotics, and steroids
Deep socket infection: Requires implant removal (responds poorly to topical/PO/IV antibiotics)

rows: Inadequate surgical closure (wound closure under tension, poor technique)
Hydroxyapatite debridement and grafting (donor sclera, fascia lata)
Dermis fat graft if orbital implant exchange fails

sections.title: Prosthesis Mobility Challenges
content: Commoner for horizontal gaze than vertical (shorter fornices)
Less common after evisceration than enucleation
Movement issue may relate to prosthesis rather than implant
Pegged implants: Higher complication rates
Treatment: Prosthetist review of fitting
Treatment: Increase size of orbital implant

sections.title: Shortening of the Fornices
content: Causes: Recurring socket infection and/or scarring 2° to trauma
Anatomy: Lower fornix shortening > Upper fornix shortening
Associations: Lower lid retraction, difficulty fitting prosthesis, prosthesis falling out
Treatment (Fornix-deepening sutures): Generally do not work
Treatment (Grafts): Amniotic Membrane Graft (AMG), hard palate, ear cartilage, or donor sclera graft
